newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks shun Dow, higher on forecast data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks shun Dow, higher on forecast data.

text.p: Mexican stocks continued a cautious but steady upward March at midday trading on Tuesday as buyers shunned a slump on Wall Street on an expected crop of strong domestic macroeconomic data, traders said.
"Volume is slow while we await the FOMC decision, but buyers are there, especially foreigners," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 20.66 points, or 0.53 percent, at 3,942.04.
"GDP data were good yesterday and we expect favorable trade balance, unemployment and inflation figures," a desk trader said.
Average trading volume of 37.9 million shares reflected investor caution ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting whose results were expected during mid-afternoon trade, traders said.
Mexico's first quarter GDP grew 5.1 percent in year-ago terms, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.

Trade balance and unemployment data for April are expected to be announced on Tuesday. A Reuters survey of Mexico City financial firms MEX22 showed they forecast a cut in unemployment and a trade surplus.
"ADRs have cut loose from the Dow, they're mostly up, as opposed to this morning," the floor trader added.
Market heavyweight Telmex ADRs were up 3/8 at 43-7/8, while the telecomms firm's L shares had gained 12 centavos to 17.30 pesos. The Dow Jones was meanwhile down 27.61 points at 7201.27 points.

Dealers drew attention to a hefty cross trade in infrequently dealt Telmex A class or preferred shares, which were up 12 centavos to 17.24 pesos. Traders said the deal was probably part of a buyback, as Telmex has corporate links with the brokerage which settled the deal.
